study.name: Using process tracing to investigate biases in decision making
study.citation: Desai, N. (2022). Using process tracing to investigate biases in decision making [Doctoral dissertation, Ohio State University]. OhioLINK ETD Center. http://rave.ohiolink.edu/etdc/view?acc_num=osu1658090359532985. Attribution from the RA compilation; the self-control experiment itself is unpublished (the dissertation PDF is embargoed and its abstract does not describe it).
study.description: Unpublished eye-tracking food-choice study with a construal (how/why) manipulation, Krajbich lab, Ohio State University (task code self_control_code_final.m).

description: Tastiness ratings, not liking: "You will now rate each individual food based on how TASTY you think the foods are. Rate each food on a scale from -10 to 10. Positive ratings are for foods that you would eat based on taste alone, while negative ratings are for foods that you would not eat based on taste alone. -10 means that the food tastes very bad. 0 means that the food tastes neither bad nor good. 10 means that the food tastes very good." (task code). 21 integer steps moved with the arrow keys from a random start (InitialTasteRate, not imported), after a slideshow of all 139 foods; TasteRating is the confirmed value. A separate health rating task (-10 very unhealthy .. 10 very healthy) is not imported. 29 participants x 139 foods (photographs of grocery products, shown at 576x432). Stimulus key: PicID indexes the task's image textures, built as [UnhealthyImages dir() list, HealthyImages dir() list] (task code lines 221-254); the two dir() lists (87 + 52 filenames) were saved in the MATLAB workspaces of participants 3, 4 and 12 (matlab3/4/12.mat in the RA's 'data (1).zip'), are identical across the three, and those workspaces' Ratings matrices [order, PicID, TasteRating, Health] equal the participants' rating CSVs row for row. The CSV Health flag equals PicID > 87 in all 4,031 rows. Item names are the image filenames, matched to existing DB items where the product is the same (46 of 139). picid_to_item.json ships the full key.
